title: ZenoX claims RedScanner group stole payment card data from SiTef servers in Brazil; institution not named
date_note: Date TechTudo published ZenoX's findings; ZenoX says the scheme was discovered on 27 October 2026. The page gives no date for the theft.
geo_basis: country stated by TechTudo; no city or institution named
summary: Security firm ZenoX says, according to TechTudo, that an attack it attributes to the group RedScanner stole data of 1.575.270 payment cards (TechTudo's figure, Brazilian notation), including CVV codes, from SiTef servers in Brazil. ZenoX says it found the scheme on 27 October 2026 and passed the records to payment companies, but kept the institution's name confidential and has no confirmation that customers were notified.
plain: A Brazilian security firm says hackers stole the details of payment cards, including CVV codes, in Brazil. The company affected has not been named and has not confirmed it.
exec: A researcher's claim of stolen card data, CVV codes included, in Brazil, unconfirmed by any institution, points to fraud risk for card issuers and merchants.
action: TechTudo's guide advises checking the invoice, contesting unknown purchases and considering blocking the card; it says the Banco Central recommends contesting the purchase and registering the occurrence through official channels.

evidence.quote: Um ataque hacker atribuído ao grupo RedScanner resultou no roubo de dados de 1.575.270 cartões de pagamento

validation.note: Only TechTudo, relaying security firm ZenoX's 'Operação Open Ledger' findings, was read; ZenoX's own report and any institution statement were not found by search. The institution is not named and has not confirmed; the RedScanner attribution is ZenoX's.

review.note: action advice: Banco Central only recommends contesting the purchase and registering the occurrence; check and block advice is TechTudo's guide; unsupported warning about check sites removed; figure, claim status and ZenoX attribution verified
